key_insight: RPG lets embodied agents improve robot execution by reconstructing skills from offline data, practicing in simulation, and retaining only validated prompt/skill updates—without changing model weights.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to continually upgrade robot autonomy while preserving a frozen policy stack, reducing the cost of retraining and simplifying deployment across tasks and hardware.
method: Mine an offline dataset to identify manipulation capabilities and generate related practice tasks in simulation.
Use execution feedback, privileged simulator state, and dataset videos to diagnose failures and create/refine symbolic skills and prompts.
Cross-test candidate revisions on held-out tasks before merging them into the reusable skill library and system prompt.
evidence_signal: On 22 held-out manipulation tasks, success rose from 28.6% after the first practice round to 95.0% after 15 rounds; after calibration, the frozen system achieved 30/30 physical trial successes across three tasks.
watch_item: The approach depends on high-quality offline data, simulator fidelity, and careful calibration/hardware adaptation, so gains may not transfer uniformly to new robots or poorly modeled environments.
paper_title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
